title: Crosswalker Tier 1
description: The canonical contract for a Crosswalker vault. Tier 1 is the load-bearing primitive: any producer (the bundled engine, an external Python script, an AI agent, an MCP server, hand-written notes) that emits files conforming to this schema produces a valid Crosswalker vault. Validation surface covers YAML frontmatter shape only — folder layout and Markdown body are recipe-defined and out of scope here. See https://crosswalker.dev/spec/recipe.schema.json for recipe shape.
$comment: v0.1. JSON Schema 2020-12. Stable URI; breaking changes will bump to /v2/. Discrimination by `kind` field: kind='junction-note' must match junction-note shape; kind='crosswalk-edge' must match crosswalk-edge shape; absent kind (or any other value) must match concept-note shape. Uses allOf+if/then so AJV can produce specific error messages from the matching branch. SchemaVer 1.4.0. Additive history: 1.1.0 (2026-08-28, Ch 43) added the optional `reviewed_against` block on junction_note_frontmatter (the control fingerprint an attestation was approved against) and the optional `review_cid` on provenance_block (the concept-side current value); 1.2.0 (2026-08-28, Ch 43) widened the crosswalk_edge_frontmatter predicate_id enum with the release-lineage pair `superseded_by` / `supersedes`. 1.3.0 (2026-08-28, Ch 43) added optional recipe-driven review_groups to concept provenance and reviewed_against so a changed whole-row fingerprint can be classified as wording, scope, or housekeeping. 1.4.0 (2026-09-06) added the optional strict `_crosswalker.recipe.recipe_document_digest` reference to the complete normalized canonical recipe used for a note. All steps are property/enum widenings only: every document that validated before still validates, so the $id is unchanged.

curie.description: Compact URI (W3C CURIE). Format: prefix:local. Prefix is lowercase ASCII alphanumeric (plus _, -). Local part allows alphanumeric, dot, underscore, hyphen, parens, slash. Examples: nist:AC-2, nist:AC-2(1), iso27001:A.9.2.1, mitre-attack:T1078, scf:IAC-21, cwk:bdfd9a (anonymous concept identity).

sha256_cid.description: Content identifier: sha256 hash of the canonical concept-identity record (sorted CURIEs + canonicalized attribute set + canonicalized relations). Stable across vault layouts because the recipe's render() output is NOT included. See target-structure synthesis log for the canonical-state hash spec.

recipe_document_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of a complete validated canonical recipe after Crosswalker normalization. The hashed bytes are the full recursively key-sorted recipe JSON, including normalized defaults, source, target, metadata, ancestry references and array order.

review_group_cids.description: Recipe-driven sub-fingerprints used only to explain an already-detected review_cid change. Wording covers body-projected source content; scope covers recipe-managed frontmatter and managed links; housekeeping covers the remaining source content. All three are required when the block is present so a partial explanation is never mistaken for a complete one.

wikilink_target.description: The exact string that goes inside [[...]]. Pass-1 Render emits absolute (full-path) form: 'Frameworks/NIST 800-53 r5/AC/AC-2'. Pass-2 link minimizer (v0.3) may downgrade to bare basename when unambiguous. Heading anchors use '#' separator: 'NIST 800-53 r5#AC-2'. May include alias via '|': 'Frameworks/NIST 800-53 r5/AC/AC-2|AC-2'.

tag_path.description: Obsidian tag path. Slash-delimited segments. Segment characters: ASCII alphanumeric, underscore, hyphen. No spaces, no parens, no leading slash. Example: 'framework/nist-800-53-r5/ac/ac-2'.

provenance_block.title: _crosswalker provenance block
provenance_block.description: Frontmatter key '_crosswalker'. Records how this note arrived in the vault. Required on any note produced by a Crosswalker producer.

spec_version.description: URI of the spec this note conforms to. Static for v0.1.

source_ref.description: Where this note came from. At least one of file/url/curie required.

curie.description: Source ontology CURIE prefix (e.g., nist:_, iso27001:_).

source_hash.description: Hash of the source file at import time. Format: 'sha256-{hex}'.

producer.description: What produced this note. Helps reconstruct provenance across producer ecosystems.

recipe.description: Reference to the recipe used to produce this note. Optional but strongly recommended for reproducibility.

hash.description: Hash of the recipe content at production time. Format: 'sha256-{hex}'.

recipe_document_digest.description: Digest of the complete normalized canonical recipe referenced by this provenance block.

import_set.description: The durable ownership set this generated note belongs to. Optional for legacy notes; all new Crosswalker emissions include it.

id.description: Crypto-random, semantically meaningless import-set identifier. Minted once and reused on refresh.

scheme.description: Identity scheme fixed when the import set is minted. endpoint-v1 identifies crosswalk assertions by endpoints. set-qualified-v1 uses cwset-<import-set-id>-<sanitized-subject>-<sanitized-object>, allowing assertions with the same endpoints in different sets to coexist without changing any existing identity.

destination.description: Folder this import set was last written to. Recorded so a refresh can find where the set already lives instead of inferring it from vault paths. A hint, not authority: a reader re-validates it against the actual note paths of the set, because nothing updates it when a user renames the folder.

ontology.description: Ontology this import set mints its CURIEs under, pinned when the set is minted, the same way scheme is. A refresh uses the pin instead of recomputing the ontology from its own recipe: a recomputation that lands on a different answer produces CURIEs matching none of the notes the set already owns, so the run writes a second copy of the whole import and reports every original as an orphan. Absent on notes written before the pin existed; such a set is pinned on its first refresh to the ontology prefix its own notes already carry.

derivation.description: Identity-derivation rule fixed when the import set is minted, the same way scheme and ontology are. filename-stem-v1 is the rule shipped since v0.1.0: the CURIE local part is the leaf filename stem passed through the filesystem sanitizer, which is many-to-one and rewrites even a declared curie column. declared-facts-v1 derives from the source's declared identity first (curie, then id, subject_id, control_id, code) and falls back to the filename stem only when none is present; a declared curie outside the CURIE charset is refused for that row rather than rewritten, and any sanitization that does happen is injective, so two distinct source values can never produce one CURIE. Absent means filename-stem-v1: every note written before this pin existed was written by that rule, and a refresh must keep using it or it recognises none of the notes the set already owns.

concept_cid.description: Content identifier of the canonical concept-identity record. Same across recipes that produce different vault layouts from identical source data.

review_cid.description: Normalized content fingerprint of this concept, computed over the same identity record as concept_cid but with the review-normalization rule applied to every string value. Cosmetically-different content (citation markers, curly quotes, collapsed whitespace, markdown link destinations) hashes identically here and differently in concept_cid. Optional; absent means the producer did not compute one, which is NOT a claim that the content is unchanged.

review_groups.description: Recipe-driven explanation hashes for this concept's current source row. They classify a changed review_cid but never replace it as the whole-row change gate.

concept_note_frontmatter.title: Concept note frontmatter
concept_note_frontmatter.description: Frontmatter shape for a Tier 1 concept note (an ontology element: control, technique, term, taxon, etc.). The body of the note is recipe-defined. Recipe-managed keys live alongside user_preserve keys; the producer must not touch user_preserve keys on re-render.

curie.description: Canonical concept identity. Stable across vault layouts.

aliases.description: Alternate names. Used by Obsidian alias resolution and external search.

tags.description: Obsidian tags. Recipe also_emit.tags or layout-level tag mechanism populates this.

parent.description: Hierarchy: parent concept(s). Single string or array (polyhierarchy). Wikilink target form.

parent_curie.description: Stable identity of the canonical parent concept. The parent wikilink remains the clickable vault address. One canonical parent identity is projected; additional display parents may remain in parent.

children.description: Hierarchy: child concepts. Optional (may be derived from parent edges).

concept_note_frontmatter.$comment: additionalProperties: true because recipes write domain-specific frontmatter (control_id, family, baseline, taxon_id, etc.) that this generic schema cannot enumerate. Recipes declare which additional keys are 'managed' (recipe-owned, overwritten on re-render) vs 'user_preserve' (user annotations, never overwritten) — see recipe.schema.json target.also_emit.frontmatter.

junction_note_frontmatter.title: Junction note frontmatter (evidence link)
junction_note_frontmatter.description: Tier 1 evidence-link note. Each junction note represents one (subject_concept, predicate, evidence_doc) triple plus its metadata. 13-field schema per Ch 07 evidence-link edge model synthesis.

curie.description: Junction note identity (typically auto-generated CWUUID-based CURIE).

kind.description: Discriminator: junction note vs concept note.

subject.description: The concept being attested to (e.g., NIST AC-2).

subject_curie.description: Stable identity of the subject concept/control being attested to. The subject wikilink remains the clickable vault address.

object.description: The evidence document (policy, audit report, runbook, etc.).

object_curie.description: Stable identity of the object evidence document. The object wikilink remains the clickable vault address.

coverage.description: Coverage assessment. 'full': evidence fully addresses the control. 'partial': addresses part. 'none': no coverage. 'n/a': not applicable.

reviewer.description: Who reviewed this evidence link (display name, ORCID, or email).

reviewed_against.description: The subject state a human approved this attestation against. Written only when a human approves; a producer must never fabricate it. Absent means no baseline was recorded, which is NOT a claim that the subject is unchanged.

curie.description: Identity of the subject as reviewed. Records WHICH subject the fingerprint was taken from, so a later rename or re-point is detectable.

review_cid.description: Normalized content fingerprint of the subject at approval time. Compared against the current _crosswalker.review_cid of the subject; a difference means the reviewed content changed and the attestation needs re-review.

review_groups.description: Optional recipe-driven explanation hashes recorded beside review_cid. Legacy baselines without this block remain valid but are classified conservatively when review_cid changes.

status.description: Lifecycle status of this evidence link.

expires_at.description: When this evidence link expires (annual review cadence, etc.).

crosswalk_edge_frontmatter.title: Crosswalk edge frontmatter (between two concepts in different ontologies)
crosswalk_edge_frontmatter.description: Tier 1 crosswalk edge. Each crosswalk note represents one (concept_a, predicate, concept_b) mapping with STRM-shaped predicate vocabulary plus SSSOM-flavored metadata. Used when crosswalks are stored as separate edge notes; alternative is to embed crosswalk wikilinks directly in concept-note frontmatter (recipe choice).

predicate_id.description: Eight Crosswalker predicates: the five set-theoretic STRM relationships from NIST IR 8477 (used by SCF/OSCAL), the Crosswalker extension is_approximate_to, and the release-lineage pair superseded_by / supersedes. Lineage is modelled as an ordinary crosswalk assertion between two release ontologies, so a rename is one edge, a split is N edges sharing subject_id, and a merge is N edges sharing object_id. Direction: subject_id superseded_by object_id means the subject is the OLD concept and the object is its replacement. Lineage predicates are NOT set-theoretic and must never be coerced into an OLIR/STRM relationship on export.

mapping_set_id.description: Stable identifier of the mapping-set release containing this assertion. Writers trim surrounding whitespace; comparison otherwise preserves the string and case exactly.

predicate_modifier.description: Explicit negation of the stated predicate. Absent means positive; NOT means the stated predicate does not hold.

mapping_provider.description: Source of the mapping (e.g., 'NIST OLIR mapping CSF-2.0_to_800-53').
